newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Lower House formally re-elects Hashimoto PM.
newsitem.headline: Japan Lower House formally re-elects Hashimoto PM.

text.p: Japan's Lower House formally re-elected Ryutaro Hashimoto prime minister on Thursday.

Hashimoto was re-elected by lawmakers at a special parliamentary session and his victory was announced to the house by Speaker Soichiro Ito. Hashimoto will head a minority government expected to be formed later in the day.

In October 20 general elections, Hashimoto's conservative Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) increased its standing in parliament's dominant Lower House but fell short of an overall majority, winning 239 of the 500 seats in the chamber.

Hashimoto plans to govern with the support of independents and in a loose alliance with his old coalition partners, the Social Democratic Party and the Sakigake party, an LDP splinter group. Their votes helped secure his re-election as prime minister, despite the LDP's lack of an overall majority. Hashimoto garnered 262 votes from the Lower House lawmakers.
Hashimoto has been prime minister since January, when he took over as the head of the now defunct coalition.

The two junior partners in the former coalition have agreed to support Hashimoto on key legislation but unlike the previous arrangement will not have members in his cabinet. Hashimoto is expected to name his new cabinet later on Thursday.
